review_notes: The target file contains a single theorem, so I searched the sibling directory for repeated machinery. The same theorem, with the same statement and proof, also appears in LocalCriterionNormalTwoFixedMaximality.lean under a different namespace. I read both copies and checked their imports. I also read the uses of each copy (LocalCriterionMaximalFixedSetTwoPoint.lean and the second theorem in LocalCriterionNormalTwoFixedMaximality.lean). Both files transitively import LocalCriterionMaximalPrimeMaximality, which defines IsMaximalPrimeMotion. The duplication is therefore removable without new import edges. I could not compile anything, so the merge is untested. Remaining uncertainty: other differences in open namespaces could cause name-resolution surprises. The statements are textually identical, and pointFixedSet, conjugacyWithin and involutionPointClass each have a single definition in the sources I grepped.

findings.problem: The whole theorem (statement and proof) is copied verbatim into LocalCriterionNormalTwoFixedMaximality.lean as `CFSG.ProperTwoGeneratedCore.LocalCriterionNormalTwoFixed.exists_maximal_full_motion`. The repeated argument is the following. First define the property "p-group, at least 3 fixed points, and some involution-class element normalizing it with full motion". Then take a maximal element above P with `Finite.exists_le_maximal`. Then unpack the property to obtain IsMaximalPrimeMotion and show that any strictly larger A with the property contradicts maximality. A fix to the maximality argument or the property would have to be made in two files. The two copies live in different namespaces, so nothing signals that they are the same result.
findings.proposed_change:
Keep one copy in the shared upstream module, LocalCriterionMaximalPrimeMaximality.lean, right after `IsMaximalPrimeMotion`. Put it in namespace `CFSG.ProperTwoGeneratedCore.LocalCriterionMaximalPrime`, with the statement exactly as above:
`theorem exists_maximal_full_motion (H P : Subgroup G) (z : G) (p : ℕ) (hP : IsPGroup p P) (hfixed : 3 ≤ Nat.card (pointFixedSet H P)) (r : G) (hr : r ∈ involutionPointClass z) (hrP : r ∈ Subgroup.normalizer (P : Set G)) (hmotion : Nat.card (conjugacyWithin P r) = p ^ (Nat.card (conjugacyWithin H z)).factorization p) : ∃ M, P ≤ M ∧ IsPGroup p M ∧ 3 ≤ Nat.card (pointFixedSet H M) ∧ IsMaximalPrimeMotion H z p M ∧ ∃ s ∈ involutionPointClass z, s ∈ Subgroup.normalizer (M : Set G) ∧ Nat.card (conjugacyWithin M s) = p ^ ... `
The proof is the existing one: define `property`, apply `Finite.exists_le_maximal`, then `refine ⟨M, hPM, hmax.1.1, hmax.1.2.1, ?_, hmax.1.2.2⟩`, `intro A hA hMA hAfixed hAmotion`, `exact (not_le_of_gt hMA) (hmax.2 ⟨hA, hAfixed, hAmotion⟩ hMA.le)`.
Delete this declaration from LocalCriterionMaximalFixedSetSelection.lean. Delete the twin from LocalCriterionNormalTwoFixedMaximality.lean. Both files already `open ...LocalCriterionMaximalPrime`. In LocalCriterionMaximalFixedSetTwoPoint.lean (`exists_maximal_full_motion H QG z p hQp (by omega) r hr hrQ hrmotion`) and in `full_motion_fixed_card_le_two` (`exists_maximal_full_motion H P z p hP (by omega) r hr hrP hmotion`) the call sites stay textually unchanged and resolve to the shared lemma. If Selection.lean becomes empty, it can be removed and the TwoPoint import redirected.
findings.benefit: The maximal-selection argument has a single definition, so a future change to IsMaximalPrimeMotion or to the motion property is made once. A reader no longer has to compare two same-named theorems in different namespaces. About 20 duplicated lines are removed, and the import graph is unchanged.
